mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.header: Heating a basin with a Furnace
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_1: A Furnace heats a basin on top of it, as a Blaze Burner would
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_2: Lit, charcoal and coal only burn Hot. That warms a basin, but too little for heated recipes like brass
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_3: A Searing fire heats it like a fed Blaze Burner. Burn Coal Coke, or fan charcoal with a Bellows
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_4: Once lit, it burns its fuel whether or not the basin holds anything, and fires its chamber meanwhile
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_5: With no mixer or press over it, a heated basin boils salt water down instead: each 500 mB leaves a lump of salt
mcremix.ponder.kiln_basin.text_6: Heat from under the furnace passes up unchanged: only fuel burnt in the furnace heats the basin harder
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_1: A campfire only heats this furnace to Warm, and copper needs Hot
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_2: While its shaft turns, a Bellows blows into the block in front of its nozzle
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_3: A furnace standing on a fanned fire burns one level hotter. This campfire now heats it to Hot, with no fuel at all
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_4: Blowing straight into a furnace works too: its fuel burns one level hotter, but twice as fast. Charcoal now reaches Searing
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_5: Bellows cannot light a furnace with no fire, and never push one past Searing. Only a superheated Blaze Burner reaches Blazing
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_6: Food on a campfire it blows into cooks twice as fast
mcremix.ponder.bellows_intro.text_7: Any speed will do. Turning it faster only puts more stress on the network
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.header: Heating a steam boiler with a Furnace
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.text_1: A Furnace heats a steam boiler on top of it, as a Blaze Burner would
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.text_2: Fuel it and light it. A Warm or Hot fire only keeps the boiler simmering, as a campfire would: the engine runs slowly and weakly
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.text_3: A Searing fire boils it like a fed Blaze Burner. Burn Coal Coke, or fan charcoal with a Bellows
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.text_4: Heat from under the furnace passes up unchanged: only fuel burnt in the furnace boils the boiler harder
mcremix.ponder.kiln_boiler.text_5: Once lit, it burns its fuel whether or not the engine is running, and fires its chamber meanwhile
mcremix.ponder.crucible.header: Melting and pouring metal with a Crucible
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_1: A Crucible melts metal with the heat beneath it
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_2: Put metal in by hand, or with funnels, chutes and arms: ingots, nuggets, sheets, and raw or crushed ore. An ingot or a piece of ore melts into 90 mB
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_3: Zinc melts Hot; copper, gold and brass Searing, over a fed Blaze Burner. Iron, steel and netherite need a superheated one
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_4: Metals that meet in it join as alloys: copper and zinc as brass, iron and coal coke as steel, gold and netherite scrap as netherite
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_5: Turning its shaft tips it over. It pours whatever rises over its lip, so tip it a little to pour a little
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_6: A Sand Mold on a depot or belt under the stream fills with one metal. Full, it sets, then the casting breaks out of the sand
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_7: A Mechanical Press rams molds in a basin: sand round an ingot, or four sand round a block. The pattern comes back out
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_8: Turn the shaft back to stand it up again
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_9: Metal that misses spills like slow lava and sets fire to what it touches, then sets as Rough Metal, which mines back into ingots
mcremix.ponder.crucible.text_10: 27 Crucibles placed as a cube join into one big crucible. It needs heat under every column, holds 27 times as much, and melts nine times as fast
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_1: Every Mechanical Drill comes with iron bits, whatever it is made of
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_2: Use stone, gold or diamond bits on a drill to fit them. The old bits pop out
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_3: A Deployer holding bits fits them too, and a drill keeps its bits when broken
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_4: Bits cut as fast as a pickaxe of their material: gold fastest, then diamond, iron and stone
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_5: They only cut what that pickaxe can mine. Gold bits cannot cut iron, copper or lapis ore
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_6: Stone bits cannot cut gold, diamond, emerald or redstone ore
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_7: Only diamond bits cut obsidian, crying obsidian and ancient debris. Iron bits no longer can
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_8: A drill on a block too hard for its bits throws sparks. Look at it to see which bits would cut it
mcremix.ponder.drill_bits.text_9: Stone and gold bits need half the stress of iron bits. Diamond bits need twice as much
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_1: An Electrolyser fixed to the side of a basin passes a heavy current through what is in it, and the current splits it
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_2: It carries the current in on two Carbon Electrodes, which stand out of its terminals. The first one fitted is the anode (+), the second the cathode (-)
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_3: Wire its + terminal to the + side of a Power Grid source and its - terminal to the - side. Wired the wrong way round, nothing flows
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_4: Below about 4 V next to nothing flows. Past that the current climbs steeply, and with it how fast it splits and how hot it runs
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_5: A generator wired straight across one drives a huge current through it and cooks it. Step the voltage down with a transformer, or wire several in series
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_6: Salt water splits into caustic soda, which stays in the basin, and chlorine and hydrogen, which escape over it
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_7: Chlorine let loose is a green cloud that hurts you and kills plants, while the hydrogen just hisses away. A vat keeps both
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_8: Alumina, put in by a funnel or an arm, splits into molten aluminium. It needs no heat under the basin: the current keeps it hot
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_9: Pipe the molten aluminium off into a crucible to cast it
mcremix.ponder.electrolyser_basin.text_1: The anode burns away with the power through it, and the cathode a tenth as fast. When one is gone, the Electrolyser stops
Fit a new one by hand, or let a funnel or an arm feed them in
Driven hard it runs hot, like any Power Grid device. A Heat Sink on top draws the heat out of it
mcremix.ponder.vat.header: Settling and electrolysis in a vat
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_1: A vat is a tank one to three wide and up to five high, standing on a whole layer of andesite scaffolding, which becomes its cone and legs
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_2: Its windows shut while it stands, and open again once it is taken apart. Engineer's Goggles show what it holds
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_3: Pipes fill it through any of its tanks, and funnels, chutes and arms put in the items it works on
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_4: Left alone it settles what will settle: a batch for every bucket it holds, all at once, where a basin settles one at a time
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_5: What it makes as items comes out of the outlet under its cone, piped to any inventory beside or under its scaffolding
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_6: A funnel on its scaffolding, facing out, pulls them out too
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_7: What it makes as liquids, like the caustic soda the liquor gives back, waits in the vat for its pipes to draw off
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_8: With Electrolysers on its sides it splits what a current splits, as fast as their current allows
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_9: In series, the - of one wired to the + of the next, they share one source. Each needs about 4 V, so two need about 8
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_10: A vat is closed, so it keeps the chlorine and hydrogen. Its pipes draw off its gases first, then its liquids
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_11: Pumped up into a Steel Furnace from underneath, hydrogen burns hotter the faster it comes, up to Blazing
mcremix.ponder.vat.text_12: Once it has no room left for what it makes, it stops until its pipes take some away
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_1: Aluminium supports warm up as they turn, the faster the hotter: an aluminium gearbox, clutch, gearshift, chain drive or machine, or an aluminium bracket or casing. Titanium ones warm up too, twice as much
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_2: Only what holds the part heats, so an aluminium shaft in a steel bracket stays cool. No other material heats up at all
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_3: Goggles show how hot it is. It takes about a minute to warm through, and left alone at 256 RPM it settles at about 600 °C, glowing and smoking from 520
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_4: Faster still, it drips from 620 °C, and at 660 it melts
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_5: The aluminium runs down and sets as rough aluminium, and the shafts it held drop off unless another support holds them
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_6: A Heat Sink bolted onto it, base down, draws the heat out into the air, so it runs whole to about 384 RPM
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_7: With no Heat Sink, an encased fan blowing straight onto it cools it about as much as one Heat Sink does
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_8: A fan of 128 RPM or more blowing through the Heat Sink's fins carries it to aluminium's top speed of 512 RPM
mcremix.ponder.friction_heat.text_9: For more, bolt a Water Cooler on in its place: it carries the heat away in water, faster than anything else
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_1: Shafts and cogs cannot hang in the air. Each needs a support to hold it
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_2: Machines, gearboxes, clutches, gearshifts, chain drives, encased shafts and cogs, and brackets are supports, and a speed controller holds the large cog on top of it
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_3: A support holds the parts in line with it, as far along as their material reaches
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_4: Wood and brass reach two blocks, andesite, copper and iron four, and steel, aluminium and titanium six
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_5: Like a torch, a part goes only where something holds it. Out of reach of every support, it will not go on
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_6: Sources hold nothing: a motor, engine, water wheel or crank only drives. Belts and gauges hold nothing either
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_7: Goggles show how far a part reaches, and which support holds it
mcremix.ponder.friction_points.text_8: Take a support away, and the parts only it held drop off
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_1: A bracket goes down on its own, bolted to a solid face: a floor, a wall, a ceiling or the top of a post. With nothing solid there, it will not go down
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_2: Place a shaft or cog into it, and it lies along the bracket, which makes it a support
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_3: A bracket also clips onto a part already placed. Its foot goes on the side away from you, here onto the top of the post
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_4: Only supports have a top speed, their Stability. A part in a bracket turns as fast as the bracket allows, whatever the part is made of
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_5: So an oak bracket holds even a copper shaft to 64 RPM. Past it, the bracket grinds and comes off. The shafts stay while another support is in reach, as the copper bracket is here
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_6: Break the block a bracket is bolted to, and the bracket falls off
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_7: Copper and iron brackets weather like their parts, and every stage adds friction
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_8: Honeycomb waxes a part and its bracket together, and an axe scrapes them together
mcremix.ponder.brackets.text_9: Hold brackets in your offhand, and one goes on each part as you place it
mcremix.ponder.encasing.text_1: Any shaft or cog goes into any material's casing: andesite, brass, copper, iron, steel, aluminium or titanium. Encased, it is a support
mcremix.ponder.encasing.text_2: The casing sets its top speed and its friction, whatever the part is made of. The part sets only the load it carries, and out of the weather it keeps the look it went in with
mcremix.ponder.encasing.text_3: Past 128 RPM this andesite casing grinds and gives way, leaving the copper shaft that was in it
mcremix.ponder.encasing.text_4: Sneak and use a wrench to take a casing off again. Encasing never uses the casing up, and breaking an encased part gives back the part inside
mcremix.ponder.wood_fuse.text_1: Every shaft and cog carries only so much stress, its Strength: wood 2,048 su, brass 3,072, copper 4,096 and aluminium 8,192. Andesite, iron, steel and titanium carry any load
mcremix.ponder.wood_fuse.text_2: Put more stress through a network than a shaft or cog carries, and it wobbles for about a second, then breaks off, bare, bracketed or encased. Supports never break from load
mcremix.ponder.wood_fuse.text_3: Wood carries the least, so it breaks first. A wooden part between your engine and a risky machine is a fuse: the overload is cut off, and the engine side keeps turning
mcremix.ponder.speed_controller.text_1: A speed controller supports the large cog in its top slot, so the cog needs no bracket
mcremix.ponder.speed_controller.text_2: Like any support, it holds the parts along the cog's axis as far as their material reaches
mcremix.ponder.speed_controller.text_3: The controller is brass, so its own shaft turns no faster than 96 RPM. The cog it drives is no support itself and has no top speed: the supports further on set it
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_1: Furnaces work differently now. There is no menu: everything happens in their two openings
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_2: Right-click the upper chamber to load things to fire
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_3: Right-click the low firebox with fuel. It does not catch by itself
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_4: Light it with Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge, by hand or from a Deployer. Wood only burns Warm, which is enough for clay and charcoal
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_5: Finished items wait inside. Take them with an empty hand, or put a hopper underneath
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_6: Sneak with an empty hand to take back anything that has not been fired yet
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_7: Once lit, it burns its fuel whether or not there is anything to fire, until the fuel runs out and the fire dies
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_8: A Shovel puts it out, by hand or from a Deployer, and leaves the fuel in for next time
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_9: Charcoal and coal burn Hot: enough for glass, copper, gold and Coal Coke
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_10: Coal Coke and Blaze Rods burn Searing, which iron needs. Engineer's Goggles show the heat and what each item still needs
mcremix.ponder.kiln_intro.text_11: Hoppers and funnels work too: items in through the top, fuel through the sides, results out the bottom
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_1: A furnace also takes heat from whatever is directly beneath it. That heat needs no fuel and no lighting
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_2: Campfires and magma give Warm heat
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_3: Fire and lava give Hot heat
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_4: A fed Blaze Burner gives Searing heat, enough to fire raw iron into blooms
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_5: Superheated with Blaze Cake, it reaches Blazing. Every level above what a recipe needs halves the time, and some recipes yield double
mcremix.ponder.kiln_heat.text_6: Power Grid's electric heaters work too, by temperature: 200°C is Warm, 400°C Hot, 600°C Searing and 1200°C Blazing
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_1: Raw iron will not melt into ingots any more. At Searing heat, a furnace fires it into a glowing Iron Bloom
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_2: A bloom is spongy iron full of slag. Strike it on an anvil to beat the slag out. Until you have iron for one, a Stone Anvil will do
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_3: Four strikes give an iron ingot, often with Slag. Slag fertilises crops like bone meal, and washing it recovers iron nuggets
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_4: Stone cracks as you work it. A Stone Anvil chips, cracks deeper, and crumbles to cobblestone after about fifteen blooms
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_5: An iron anvil costs 31 iron, but it wears down about seven times more slowly
mcremix.ponder.iron_bloom.text_6: A Mechanical Press hammers blooms automatically. At Blazing heat, crushed iron fires into two blooms instead of one
mcremix.ponder.cementation.text_1: Steel is iron that has soaked up carbon. Pack four iron ingots in four coal coke and seal them with a clay ball, and you have a Cementation Pack
mcremix.ponder.cementation.text_2: Fire it at Searing heat, from any heat source. It is the slowest firing there is, as the carbon creeps into the iron
mcremix.ponder.cementation.text_3: Each pack comes out as four Blister Steel
mcremix.ponder.cementation.text_4: Blister steel is brittle, its skin raised in blisters where the carbon went in. Only a Mechanical Press can beat it into steel ingots
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.header: Cooling Power Grid devices with a Heat Sink
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.text_1: Power Grid's devices heat up with the current through them, and burn out if they get too hot
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.text_2: A Heat Sink draws heat out of the device its base sits on, and its aluminium fins shed it into the air
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.text_3: The device runs cooler, so it can take more power before it burns out
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.text_4: Air blown along the fins by a fan carries the heat away much faster
mcremix.ponder.heat_sink.text_5: Only the base draws heat: a sink beside a device, or with its base turned away, does nothing
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_1: Each line is held by brackets of its own material. A support's material sets its top speed, its Stability: wood 64 RPM, brass 96, andesite 128, copper and iron 256, steel and aluminium 512, titanium 2048
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_2: Only supports are held to it, here the brackets, and a part in one turns as fast as the support allows. The bare parts between them take any speed
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_3: Spin a support past its limit and it grinds, smoking or sparking, then gives way. Here every oak bracket comes off, and the oak shafts they held drop
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_4: Copper parts and brackets oxidize like copper blocks, within a day, each stopping at a stage of its own. At a support, each stage adds friction, which uses up stress
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_5: Wax them with honeycomb to keep them as they are. An axe scrapes off wax, then patina
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_6: Iron rusts the same way, but only where it gets wet. Iron supports are a little heavier to turn, and no load is too much for iron
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_7: Brass parts are delicate clockwork. They never tarnish, but they are only a little stronger than wood
mcremix.ponder.kinetic_tiers.text_8: Shafts and cogs have a Strength, the load they carry. Put more stress through a wooden, brass, copper or aluminium one than it carries and it wobbles loose and breaks
mcremix.ponder.steel_parts.text_1: Copper and iron supports top out at 256 RPM. Steel brackets, casings, gearboxes, clutches, gearshifts and chain drives run up to 512
mcremix.ponder.steel_parts.text_2: Past 256 RPM the iron brackets grind and give way, and the iron line drops, while the steel one carries on
mcremix.ponder.steel_parts.text_3: A machine draws stress for every RPM, so at 512 it works twice as fast for twice the stress. Speed only pays where it matters
mcremix.ponder.steel_parts.text_4: Steel supports are the heaviest to turn, and steel rusts as iron does, only where it gets wet. Wax it with honeycomb
mcremix.ponder.steel_parts.text_5: Steel Casing is made the way Create makes its casings, a steel sheet applied to a stripped log. Steel cased parts are built on it, and it encases any shaft or cog
mcremix.ponder.wooden_parts.text_1: Wooden shafts, gearboxes, clutches, gearshifts and brackets come in every wood, so they can match what they are built into
mcremix.ponder.wooden_parts.text_2: Only the look changes. Wooden supports top out at 64 RPM, and wood carries the least load, so it gives way first
mcremix.ponder.wooden_parts.text_3: Crimson and warped parts are cut from stems, and like the stems they do not burn
mcremix.ponder.gearbox_tiers.text_1: Gearboxes come in the same materials as shafts and cogs, with the same limits. A gearbox is a support for the shafts around it
mcremix.ponder.gearbox_tiers.text_2: Create's own gearbox is andesite, so it tops out at 128 RPM. When it breaks, the shafts it held drop off with it
mcremix.ponder.gearbox_tiers.text_3: Copper and iron gearboxes take up to 256 RPM. They oxidize and rust like their shafts, and wax the same way
mcremix.ponder.gearbox_tiers.text_4: A wooden gearbox needs no andesite. Wood carries the least load, so it gives way first when a network draws too much
mcremix.ponder.gearbox_tiers.text_5: Placed against a shaft above or below, a gearbox lies on its side to meet it. Sneak while placing to lay it down anywhere
mcremix.ponder.clutch_tiers.text_1: Clutches and gearshifts come in the same materials as gearboxes, with the same limits, all but brass. Each is a support
mcremix.ponder.clutch_tiers.text_2: Create's own clutch and gearshift are andesite, so they top out at 128 RPM. When one breaks, the shafts it held drop off with it
mcremix.ponder.clutch_tiers.text_3: Copper and iron ones take up to 256 RPM. They oxidize and rust like their shafts, and wax the same way
mcremix.ponder.clutch_tiers.text_4: Powered, a clutch of any material cuts off the far side...
mcremix.ponder.clutch_tiers.text_6: A wooden clutch is the cheapest switch. Wood carries the least load, so it gives way first when a network draws too much
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive_tiers.text_1: Chain drives come in brass, copper, iron and steel too. Each is a support, with its material's top speed
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive_tiers.text_2: Create's own chain drive and chain gearshift are andesite, so they top out at 128 RPM. Shafts only a broken one held drop off
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive_tiers.text_3: Copper and iron ones take up to 256 RPM, and one row can mix them. They oxidize and rust like their shafts, and wax the same way
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive_tiers.text_4: Powered, a chain gearshift drives the rest of its row up to twice as fast, so every chain drive past it must take the faster speed
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive_tiers.text_5: Goggles on a powered chain gearshift show how much faster the rest of its row turns
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_1: Presses, mixers, millstones, fans, saws, drills, deployers and arms also come in copper, iron, steel, aluminium and titanium. Create's own are andesite, its arm brass, and its crafter comes in brass alone
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_2: Each machine is a support, held to the top speed of its material: brass 96 RPM, andesite 128, copper and iron 256, steel and aluminium 512, titanium 2048
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_3: Spin one past its limit and it grinds, then breaks and drops. Past 128 RPM the andesite press gives way
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_4: Use a casing on a placed machine to make it that material. It keeps its facing and what it holds, and the casing it had pops out
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_5: Any casing works on any machine that comes in its material, a step down as well as up
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_6: Copper machines oxidize like copper blocks, and iron and steel ones rust where they get wet. Each stage adds a little friction, which uses up stress
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_7: Wax one with honeycomb to keep it as it is. An axe scrapes off wax, then patina
mcremix.ponder.machine_tiers.text_8: Each is crafted as Create's machine is, with its material's casing in place of the andesite or brass one. Aluminium and titanium never weather
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_1: A Pressurizer squeezes the fluid piped into it. Its shaft works a pump in the lower block, and what it squeezes is held in the vessel on top
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_2: Its shaft goes in at either side of the lower block, left or right of the dial. The faster it turns, the harder it squeezes
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_3: The dial on its front reads the pressure, which is speed. Each mark is a quarter of its top speed, 128 RPM for steel, and past 512 RPM the needle is in the red
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_4: Each job needs a speed: 128 RPM for steam, 256 for PVC resin and 512 for polyethylene. Below it nothing happens, and above it the work goes faster
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_5: It is heavy to turn: 32 stress units for every RPM, over 16,000 at 512 RPM. Gear it up, as a large cogwheel turns a small one at twice its speed
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_6: Pipe the fluid into any side of its vessel, which reaches out to meet the pipe. The vessel's top and the lower block take no pipes
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_7: At 512 RPM, over Warm heat or hotter, it sets ethylene into Polyethylene Pellets, 100 mB a batch
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_8: Take what it makes with an empty hand, or with a funnel on any side of its vessel
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_9: At 256 RPM, with or without heat underneath, it sets vinyl chloride into PVC Resin
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_10: At 128 RPM over Hot heat it turns water into pressurised steam, 20 mB a tick, and more the faster it turns
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_11: Pressurised steam is all a steel boiler runs on, with no water or fire. Every 10 mB a tick piped in is one boiler level
mcremix.ponder.pressurizer.text_12: Too slow or too cold, it waits. Engineer's Goggles show what it is waiting for
mcremix.ponder.saw_blades.text_1: Like drill bits, saw blades can be stone, iron, gold or diamond. Every saw comes with an iron blade
mcremix.ponder.saw_blades.text_2: Use another blade on a saw to fit it, or have a Deployer do it. The old blade pops out
mcremix.ponder.saw_blades.text_3: Every blade cuts wood. Gold is the fastest, then diamond, iron and stone
mcremix.ponder.saw_blades.text_4: Gold is too soft for stone: it skates across the blade uncut, in a shower of sparks
mcremix.ponder.saw_blades.text_5: Stone and gold blades take half the stress of iron, diamond twice as much. A saw keeps its blade when broken
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.header: Lighting a furnace with a Spark Plug
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_1: Furnaces and Steel Furnaces have to be lit. A Spark Plug lights one with electricity, with no one there to strike a flame
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_2: It screws into a furnace's side or back. It will not go on the front, where the fuel goes in
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_3: Wire it into a Power Grid circuit: + to the copper core on its cap, - to its iron shell
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_4: With about 1,000 V across it, it sparks and lights the fuel in the furnace. A transformer can step a lower voltage up to that
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_5: Below 900 V nothing crosses its gap. Once it sparks, it keeps on until the voltage falls below 800 V
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_6: It sparks the whole time it is powered, lit furnace or not, drawing about 10 mA. A switch or relay in its circuit decides when
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_7: Put out with a Shovel, a furnace with a sparking plug catches again at once
mcremix.ponder.spark_plug.text_8: A Spark Plug never wears out
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine_metals.heade: Steam engines in every boiler metal
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine_metals.text_: Every metal whose tanks make a boiler has a Steam Engine of its own: copper, which is Create's, brass, iron and steel
Each goes only on tanks of its own metal, as Create's goes only on its copper ones
Aluminium tanks make no boiler, so there is no aluminium engine
Whatever its metal, an engine runs as Create's does, as fast and as strong from each level of its boiler
The metal changes the boiler. Brass and iron boilers work as copper ones do, and hold fluids as hot
A steel boiler boils no water and wants no fire: it runs only on pressurised steam piped in from a Pressurizer
It is compact, a level for every two tanks, but steam its engines do not use builds pressure. Give it a whistle to vent, or it bursts
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.header: Burning piped fuel in a Steel Furnace
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_1: Steel Casing used on a Furnace cases it in steel. It keeps what it held, but its solid fuel pops out and its fire goes out
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_2: A Steel Furnace burns no solid fuel. It is sealed, so heat from underneath does not reach it, and Bellows do nothing for it
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_3: It burns fuel pumped up into it from underneath: wood spirit, ethanol, coal tar, hydrogen or ethylene
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_4: Fuel pumped into it while it is out escapes from the front. Liquids pour out, to be cleaned up, and gases hiss away into the air
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_5: Light it as you would a Furnace: Flint and Steel, a Fire Charge or a Spark Plug
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_6: Lit, it burns the fuel as it comes, and the faster it comes the hotter it burns. A pump moves 1 mB a tick for every 2 RPM, so coal tar at 4 RPM burns Searing
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_7: Each fuel stops at its own top heat, coal tar at Searing. Fuel that comes faster than that is lost, and the chimney smokes black
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_8: Coal tar goes the furthest. Only hydrogen and ethylene burn Blazing
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_9: A second after its fuel stops coming, it goes out and has to be lit again
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_10: It works fluids too, piped or poured in at its front, sides or top. What it makes waits inside for pipes to draw off
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_11: Ethanol run over Alumina in its chamber, Hot or hotter, turns to ethylene. The alumina wears away slowly
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_12: At Searing it cracks ethylene dichloride into vinyl chloride, giving off hydrogen chloride
mcremix.ponder.steel_furnace.text_13: It fires what a Furnace fires, and heats a boiler or basin on top of it the same way
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.header: Drawing off coal tar and wood spirit
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.text_1: Coking coal gives off coal tar, which collects inside the Furnace
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.text_2: Pump it off from any side, or fill a bucket from it. A Furnace takes nothing in by pipe: only a Steel Furnace burns piped fuel, from underneath
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.text_3: Charring logs gives off wood spirit the same way. The tank already holds tar, so the spirit waits in the Furnace
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.text_4: A Furnace holds a bucket of one of them. Past that, or if it holds the other one, the rest burns away at the chimney in black smoke
mcremix.ponder.kiln_byproducts.text_5: The firing carries on either way: only what it gives off is lost
mcremix.ponder.bakelite.text_1: Coal tar and wood spirit, 100 mB of each, set hard into Bakelite when pressed together in a heated basin
mcremix.ponder.bakelite.text_2: Power Grid's blank circuit boards are sawn from Bakelite, and its switches, buttons and sockets need it too
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_1: Titanium is the fastest material of all: its supports take up to 2048 RPM, under any load
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_2: Like aluminium they warm up as they turn, but twice as much, so they need twice the cooling. With nothing on it this gearbox holds about 128 RPM
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_3: Heat leaves its colours on it, as on real titanium: past 400 °C what holds the part turns gold, past 550 purple and past 700 blue
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_4: The colour stays when it cools, a record of how hot it has run. Only hydrochloric acid strips it back to plain titanium
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_5: Run it too hot and past 1000 °C it burns: it flares white for a few seconds, setting fire to anything that burns across the gap beside it
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_6: Then it crumbles into titanium dioxide, which does for rutile again. What it held drops off unless another support holds it
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_7: Cool it with water: a Water Cooler on water holds it to about 700 RPM, on cold water 1300 and on coolant 1900. Its top speed takes two coolers of coolant
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_8: A Heat Sink is little use on it: the sink melts past 660 °C, so it holds titanium only to about 150 RPM, or 225 with a fan through it
mcremix.ponder.titanium_heat.text_9: Titanium plating, for building with, takes the same colours from a Furnace: gold at Hot, purple at Searing and blue at Blazing
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.header: Melting titanium in the Arc Furnace
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_1: The Arc Furnace melts titanium sponge into ingots. Molten titanium dissolves any crucible, so it melts on a copper hearth kept cool
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_2: Fit a Carbon Electrode under each terminal. The arc runs down one, through what lies in the hearth, and back up the other
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_3: Wire its two terminals across a Power Grid source, either way round. The arc is a heavy load of a quarter ohm: 20 V drive 80 A, 1.6 kW
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_4: It melts nothing below 400 W, and its hearth sheds only 150 W by itself, so working on its own it soon overheats
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_5: A Water Cooler bolted onto it takes the heat away. One on water holds it to about 2.5 kW
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_6: Put the sponge in by hand, funnel or arm. Each takes 16 kJ to melt, and a hopper below takes the ingots out
mcremix.ponder.arc_furnace.text_7: Both electrodes burn away as it works, each lasting 160 kJ. When one is gone, the arc goes out until a new one is fitted
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_1: A vat holds up to four fluids at once, each in a layer of its own: the heaviest at the bottom and gases at the top. Engineer's Goggles show them all
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_2: Use a Copper Mechanical Mixer on the side of one of its tanks, and it goes on as a plate of the vat's own tank with a cog on its face, as though put inside
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_3: A mixer only fits a vat of its own material: copper on copper vats, iron on iron, steel on steel and aluminium on aluminium. Create's own mixer works only over basins, and no mixer fits a brass vat. Sneak to put down an ordinary mixer instead
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_4: No shaft goes into it: its cog turns with the cogs beside it, as a Mechanical Mixer's does. Turned, it stirs what the vat holds, four batches at a time. A big vat wants several mixers
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_5: Chlorine and ethylene stirred over a little ferric chloride make ethylene dichloride, for a Steel Furnace to crack into vinyl chloride
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_6: A vat mixes only wet, unheated recipes. Nothing settles or ferments in it while its mixers turn
mcremix.ponder.vat_mixer.text_7: Pipes on any of its tanks draw off what it makes, gases first, and leave what it is still using
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_1: A Water Cooler bolts on like a Heat Sink, its base against an aluminium or titanium support or a Power Grid device
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_2: Pipe water through it, in at any face but its base. It takes the heat in step with how hot what it cools is, and gives the water back warm
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_3: Pump the warm water away, or the cooler stops when it is full
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_4: A Radiator chills any water into cold water. Radiators side by side facing the same way join into one panel that shares what it holds
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_5: Pipes join the panel on its front or back, on any of its blocks
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_6: On its own it chills slowly. A fan under each column, blowing up through it, makes the whole column chill much faster
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_7: Pump the cold water back into the cooler to close the loop. Cold water takes heat twice as fast as water
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_8: Water taken wherever it snows is already cold. Poured out, warm or cold water is only water
mcremix.ponder.water_cooling.text_9: Coolant, glycol mixed with water, takes heat three times as fast as water. It comes out hot, a Radiator cools it back, and it never wears out, so keep it going round a loop
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press.header: Processing Items with the Mechanical Press
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press.text_1: The Mechanical Press can process items provided beneath it
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press.text_2: The Input items can be dropped or placed on a Depot under the Press
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press.text_3: When items are provided on a belt...
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press.text_4: The Press will hold and process them automatically
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_press_compacti: Compacting items with the Mechanical Press
Pressing items held in a Basin will cause them to be Compacted
Compacting includes any filled 2x2 or 3x3 Crafting Recipe, plus a couple extra ones
Some of those recipes may require the heat of a Blaze Burner
The filter slot can be used in case two recipes are conflicting.
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_mixer.header: Processing Items with the Mechanical Mixer
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_mixer.text_1: With a Mixer and Basin, some Crafting Recipes can be automated
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_mixer.text_2: Available recipes include any Shapeless Crafting Recipe, plus a couple extra ones
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_mixer.text_3: Some of those recipes may require the heat of a Blaze Burner
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_mixer.text_4: The filter slot can be used in case two recipes are conflicting.
mcremix.ponder.millstone.text_1: Millstones process items by grinding them
mcremix.ponder.millstone.text_2: They can be powered from the side using cogwheels
mcremix.ponder.millstone.text_3: Throw or Insert items at the top
mcremix.ponder.millstone.text_4: After some time, the result can be obtained via Right-click
mcremix.ponder.millstone.text_5: The outputs can also be extracted by automation
mcremix.ponder.fan_direction.text_1: Encased Fans use Rotational Force to create an Air Current
mcremix.ponder.fan_direction.text_2: Strength and Direction of Flow depends on the Rotational Input
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_1: When passing through lava, the Air Flow becomes Heated
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_2: Items caught in the area will be smelted
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_3: Food items thrown here would be incinerated
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_4: Instead, a setup for Smoking using Fire should be used for them
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_5: Air Flows passing through water create a Washing Setup
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_6: Some interesting new processing can be done with it
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_7: The Speed of the Fan does NOT affect the processing speed, only its range
mcremix.ponder.fan_processing.text_8: Fan Processing can also be applied to Items on Depots and Belts
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_saw_processing: Processing Items on the Mechanical Saw
Upward facing Mechanical Saws can process a variety of items
The processed item always moves against the rotational input to the saw
Saws can work in-line with Mechanical Belts
When an ingredient has multiple possible outcomes, the filter slot can specify it
Without filter, the Saw would cycle through all outcomes instead
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_saw_breaker.he: Cutting Trees with the Mechanical Saw
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_saw_breaker.te: When given Rotational Force, a Mechanical Saw will cut trees directly in front of it
In order to cut the tree fully, the Saw has to break the last block connecting it to the ground
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_saw_contraptio: Whenever Saws are moved as part of an animated Contraption...
...they will cut any trees the contraption runs them into
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_drill.header: Breaking Blocks with the Mechanical Drill
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_drill.text_1: When given Rotational Force, a Mechanical Drill will break blocks directly in front of it
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_drill.text_2: Its mining speed depends on the Rotational Input
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_drill_contrapt: Whenever Drills are moved as part of an animated Contraption...
...they will break blocks the contraption runs them into
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_1: Given Rotational Force, a Deployer can imitate player interactions
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_2: It will always interact with the position 2 blocks in front of itself
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_3: Blocks directly in front will not obstruct it
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_10: Right-click the front to give it an Item to use
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_11: Items can also be inserted automatically
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_13: When a filter is set, it activates only while holding a matching item
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_14: Only items matching the filter can now be inserted...
mcremix.ponder.deployer.text_15: ...and only non-matching items will be extracted
mcremix.ponder.deployer_modes.text_1: By default, a Deployer imitates a Right-click interaction
mcremix.ponder.deployer_modes.text_2: Using a Wrench, it can be set to imitate a Left-click instead
mcremix.ponder.deployer_processing.text_: With a fitting held item, Deployers can process items provided beneath them
The Input items can be dropped or placed on a Depot under the Deployer
When items are provided on a belt...
The Deployer will hold and process them automatically
mcremix.ponder.deployer_redstone.text_1: When powered by Redstone, Deployers will not activate
mcremix.ponder.deployer_redstone.text_2: Before stopping, the Deployer will finish any started cycles
mcremix.ponder.deployer_redstone.text_3: Thus, a negative pulse can be used to trigger exactly one activation cycle
mcremix.ponder.deployer_contraption.head: Using Deployers on Contraptions
mcremix.ponder.deployer_contraption.text: Whenever Deployers are moved as part of an animated Contraption...
They activate at each visited location, using items from inventories anywhere on the contraption
The Filter slot can be used to specify which items to pull
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_1: An array of Mechanical Crafters can be used to automate any Crafting Recipe
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_2: Using a Wrench, the Crafters' paths can be arranged
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_3: For a valid setup, all paths have to converge into one exit at any side
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_4: The outputs will be placed into the inventory at the exit
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_5: Mechanical Crafters require Rotational Force to operate
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_6: Right-Click the front to insert Items manually
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_7: Once every slot of a path contains an Item, the crafting process will begin
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter.text_8: For recipes not fully occupying the crafter setup, the start can be forced using a Redstone Pulse
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter_connec: Items can be inserted to Crafters automatically
Using the Wrench at their backs, Mechanical Crafter inputs can be combined
All connected Crafters can now be accessed by the same input location
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_crafter_covers: Some recipes will require additional Crafters to bridge gaps in the path
Using Slot Covers, Crafters can be set to act as an Empty Slot in the arrangement
Shared Inputs created with the Wrench at the back can also reach across covered Crafters
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_1: Mechanical Arms have to be assigned their in- and outputs before they are placed
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_2: Right-Click inventories while holding the Arm to assign them as Targets
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_3: Right-Click again to toggle between Input (Blue) and Output (Yellow)
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_4: Left-Click components to remove their Selection
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_5: Once placed, the Mechanical Arm will target the blocks selected previously
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_6: They can have any amount of in- and outputs within their range
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_7: However, not every type of Inventory can be interacted with directly
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm.text_8: Funnels and Depots can help to Bridge that gap
Filtering Outputs of the Mechanical Arm
Sometimes it is desirable to restrict targets of the Arm by matching a filter
Mechanical Arms by themselves do not provide any options for filtering
Brass Funnels as Targets do however communicate their own filter to the Arm
The Arm is smart enough not to pick up items it couldn't distribute
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm_modes.head: Distribution modes of the Mechanical Arm
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm_modes.text: Whenever an Arm has to choose between multiple valid outputs...
...it will act according to its setting
The value panel will allow you to configure it
Round Robin mode simply cycles through all outputs that are available
If an output is unable to take more items, it will be skipped
Forced Round Robin mode will never skip outputs, and instead wait until they are free
Prefer First prioritizes the outputs selected earliest when configuring this Arm
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_arm_redstone.t: When powered by Redstone, Mechanical Arms will not activate
Before stopping, it will finish any started cycles
Thus, a negative pulse can be used to trigger exactly one activation cycle
mcremix.ponder.clutch.header: Controlling rotational force using a Clutch
mcremix.ponder.clutch.text_1: Clutches will relay rotation in a straight line
mcremix.ponder.clutch.text_2: When powered by Redstone, it breaks the connection
mcremix.ponder.gearshift.header: Controlling rotational force using a Gearshift
mcremix.ponder.gearshift.text_1: Gearshifts will relay rotation in a straight line
mcremix.ponder.gearshift.text_2: When powered by Redstone, it reverses the transmission
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive.header: Relaying rotational force with Chain Drives
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive.text_1: Chain Drives relay rotation to each other in a row
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive.text_2: All shafts connected like this will rotate in the same direction
mcremix.ponder.chain_drive.text_3: Any part of the row can be rotated by 90 degrees
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.header: Controlling rotational speed with Chain Gearshifts
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_1: Unpowered Chain Gearshifts behave exactly like Chain Drives
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_2: When Powered, the speed transmitted to other Chain Drives in the row is doubled
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_3: Whenever the Powered Gearshift is not at the source, its speed will be halved instead
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_4: In both cases, Chain Drives in the row always run at 2x the speed of the Powered Gearshift
mcremix.ponder.chain_gearshift.text_5: Using analog signals, the ratio can be adjusted more precisely between 1 and 2
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_1: Mechanical Pistons can move blocks in front of them
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_2: Speed and direction of movement depend on the Rotational Input
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_piston.text_3: Sticky Mechanical Pistons can pull the attached blocks back
mcremix.ponder.piston_pole.text_1: Without attached Poles, a Mechanical Piston cannot move
mcremix.ponder.piston_pole.text_2: The Length of pole added at its back determines the Extension Range
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_piston_modes.h: Movement Modes of the Mechanical Piston
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_piston_modes.t: Whenever Pistons stop moving, the moved structure reverts to blocks
It can be configured never to revert to solid blocks, or only at the location it started at
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley.text_1: Rope Pulleys can move blocks vertically when given Rotational Force
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley.text_2: Direction and Speed of movement depend on the Rotational Input
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.header: Movement Modes of the Rope Pulley
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.text_1: Whenever Pulleys stop moving, the moved structure reverts to blocks
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_modes.text_2: It can be configured never to revert to solid blocks, or only at the location it started at
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_attachment.he: Moving Pulleys as part of a Contraption
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_attachment.te: Whenever Pulleys are themselves being moved by a Contraption...
...its attached structure will be dragged with it
Mind that pulleys are only movable while stopped
mcremix.ponder.rope_pulley_multi_rope.te: Whenever a pulley assembles a contraption...
...other pulleys on the same layer will connect to the structure
They do not require to be powered, the effect is purely cosmetic
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_bearing.header: Moving Structures using the Mechanical Bearing
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_bearing.text_1: Mechanical Bearings attach to the block in front of them
mcremix.ponder.mechanical_bearing.text_2: Upon receiving Rotational Force, it will assemble it into a Rotating Contraption
mcremix.ponder.bearing_modes.header: Movement Modes of the Mechanical Bearing
mcremix.ponder.bearing_modes.text_1: When Stopped, the Bearing will place the structure at the nearest grid-aligned Angle
mcremix.ponder.bearing_modes.text_2: It can be configured never to revert to solid blocks, or only near the angle it started at
mcremix.ponder.stabilized_bearings.text_: Whenever Mechanical Bearings are themselves part of a moving Structure..
..they will attempt to keep themselves upright
Once again, the bearing will attach to the block in front of it
As a result, the entire sub-Contraption will stay upright
mcremix.ponder.gantry_shaft.text_1: Gantry Shafts form the basis of a gantry setup. Attached Carriages will move along them.
mcremix.ponder.gantry_shaft.text_2: Gantry setups can move attached Blocks.
mcremix.ponder.gantry_carriage.text_1: Gantry Carriages can mount to and slide along a Gantry Shaft.
mcremix.ponder.gantry_carriage.text_2: Gantry setups can move attached Blocks.
mcremix.ponder.gantry_redstone.text_1: Redstone-powered gantry shafts stop moving their carriages
mcremix.ponder.gantry_redstone.text_2: Instead, its rotational force is relayed to the carriages' output shaft
mcremix.ponder.gantry_direction.text_1: Gantry Shafts can have opposite orientations
mcremix.ponder.gantry_direction.text_2: The movement direction of carriages depend on their shafts' orientation
mcremix.ponder.gantry_direction.text_3: ...as well as the rotation direction of the shaft
mcremix.ponder.gantry_direction.text_4: Same rules apply for the propagated rotation
mcremix.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_1: Gantry shafts attach to a carriage without the need of super glue
mcremix.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_2: Same applies for carriages on moved Gantry Shafts
mcremix.ponder.gantry_cascaded.text_3: Thus, a gantry system can be cascaded to cover multiple axes of movement
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_1: Steam Engines can be placed on a Fluid Tank of their own metal
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_2: Clicking the engine with a Shaft creates the Kinetic Output
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_3: With sufficient Heat, Water and Boiler space...
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_5: The minimal setup requires 4 Fluid Tanks
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_6: With the help of Blaze Burners, the power output can be increased
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_7: Higher power levels require more Water, Size and Heat
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_8: The boiler's current power level can be inspected with Engineer's Goggles
mcremix.ponder.steam_engine.text_9: With each added power level, an additional Engine can output at full capacity
mcremix.ponder.shared.behaviour_modify_v: This behaviour can be modified using the value panel
mcremix.ponder.shared.movement_anchors: With the help of Super Glue, larger structures can be moved.
mcremix.ponder.shared.storage_on_contrap: Inventories attached to the Contraption will pick up their drops automatically
mcremix.boiler.venting: Venting spare steam through its whistle
mcremix.boiler.building: Steam for %s more engines is building pressure
death.attack.mcremix.scalding: %1$s was scalded by a bursting boiler
death.attack.mcremix.scalding.player: %1$s was scalded by a bursting boiler while fighting %2$s
block.mcremix.rough_iron.tooltip.summary: Molten iron that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the iron back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_gold.tooltip.summary: Molten gold that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the gold back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_copper.tooltip.summa: Molten copper that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the copper back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_zinc.tooltip.summary: Molten zinc that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the zinc back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_brass.tooltip.summar: Molten brass that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the brass back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_steel.tooltip.summar: Molten steel that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the steel back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_netherite.tooltip.su: Molten netherite that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the netherite back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.rough_aluminium.tooltip.su: Molten aluminium that _set where it spilled_. Mine it for the aluminium back: an ingot for every _90 mB_ in it, the rest as nuggets.
block.mcremix.brass_fluid_pipe.tooltip.s: Thin and fine, like brass clockwork, and holds fluids up to _Hot_, like lava. A line with a brass pipe in it carries only _half_ as much.
block.mcremix.brass_mechanical_pump.tool: Turns no faster than _96 RPM_, like every brass support. Holds fluids up to _Hot_.
Sets the _most it lets through_, from _1 to 24 mB a tick_, all it moves at 96 RPM. _Hold right-click_ on the handwheel to set it.
block.mcremix.brass_fluid_tank.tooltip.s: Holds fluids up to _Hot_ and makes a _boiler_ as Create's tanks do, for _Brass Steam Engines_. Brass tanks make a vat like any other, but _no mixer_ fits one.
block.mcremix.iron_fluid_pipe.tooltip.su: Holds fluids up to _Hot_, like copper. Left wet it _rusts_, and rusted through it _drips_; with the _rustedIronLeaks_ setting on it _leaks_ too, _1 mB a tick_ for every rusted block while fluid goes through. Scrape it with an _axe_, clean it with _acid_ or _wax_ it to stop that.
block.mcremix.iron_mechanical_pump.toolt: Turns up to _256 RPM_ like Create's, and holds fluids up to _Hot_. Left wet it _rusts_, and rusted through it _drips_; with the _rustedIronLeaks_ setting on it _leaks_ too, _1 mB a tick_ for every rusted block while fluid goes through. Scrape it with an _axe_, clean it with _acid_ or _wax_ it to stop that.
block.mcremix.iron_fluid_tank.tooltip.su: Holds fluids up to _Hot_ and makes a _boiler_ as Create's tanks do, for _Iron Steam Engines_. Left wet it _rusts_, and rusted through it _drips_; with the _rustedIronLeaks_ setting on it _leaks_ too, _1 mB a tick_ for every rusted block while it holds anything. Scrape it with an _axe_, clean it with _acid_ or _wax_ it to stop that.
block.mcremix.aluminium_fluid_pipe.toolt: Light and soft. Never weathers, but holds fluids only up to _Warm_: with anything _Hot_ inside or beside it (lava, fire, a lit Furnace, a Blaze Burner, molten metal) it _melts_ into rough aluminium.
Turns up to _512 RPM_ on a _polyethylene bushing_, and _heats up_ turning fast, as aluminium supports do. Never weathers, but holds fluids only up to _Warm_: with anything _Hot_ inside or beside it (lava, fire, a lit Furnace, a Blaze Burner, molten metal) it _melts_ into rough aluminium.
block.mcremix.aluminium_fluid_tank.toolt: Makes _no boiler_, so no steam engine goes on it, and a vat of aluminium tanks takes only an _aluminium mixer_. Never weathers, but holds fluids only up to _Warm_: with anything _Hot_ inside or beside it (lava, fire, a lit Furnace, a Blaze Burner, molten metal) it _melts_ into rough aluminium.
block.mcremix.glass_pipe.tooltip.summary: Shows the fluid _running through it_ and never corrodes, but carries only _a quarter_ as much as copper. Holds fluids up to _Hot_, like lava.
block.mcremix.steel_fluid_pipe.tooltip.s: Holds fluids up to _Searing_: molten copper, gold and brass. Iron, steel and netherite are too hot for any pipe: _pour_ them from a crucible. Left wet it gets _spotted with rust_, but never worse, so it never leaks. _Wax_ it to keep it bright.
block.mcremix.steel_mechanical_pump.tool: Turns up to _512 RPM_, twice what Create's pump takes, and holds fluids up to _Searing_. Left wet it gets _spotted with rust_, but never worse, so it never leaks. _Wax_ it to keep it bright.
block.mcremix.steel_fluid_tank.tooltip.s: Holds fluids up to _Searing_. As a boiler for _Steel Steam Engines_ it boils no water and wants no fire: it runs only on _pressurised steam_ piped in, every _10 mB a tick_ a level. It is _compact_, a level for every _two_ tanks, but steam its engines do not use builds _pressure_. Left wet it gets _spotted with rust_, but never worse, so it never leaks. _Wax_ it to keep it bright.
block.mcremix.steel_fluid_tank.tooltip.b: The whistle _vents_ the spare steam, screaming.
It hisses and groans, then _bursts_: its tanks fall, what they held is lost and the steam _scalds_ whoever is near.
block.mcremix.crucible.tooltip.summary: Melts metal, ore, and metal _tools and armour_ (into half their metal) with the heat _underneath_ it, and _tips over_ as its shaft turns to pour. _27 placed as a cube_ join into one big crucible.
block.mcremix.crucible.tooltip.behaviour: Zinc and aluminium melt _Hot_; copper, gold and brass _Searing_; iron, steel and netherite need a _superheated_ Blaze Burner. A big crucible needs heat under _every column_, and melts nine times as fast.

_A full turn_ lays it on its side, and turning back stands it up. It pours whatever rises _over the lip_ onto what is in front: a _sand mold_ on a depot or belt, a tank, another crucible, or the ground.
_Copper and zinc_ join as brass; _iron and coal coke_ as steel; _gold and netherite scrap_ as netherite.
item.mcremix.unfired_crucible.tooltip.su: Clay shaped into a pot. Fire it _Hot_ in a furnace for a _Crucible_.
item.mcremix.sand_ingot_mold.tooltip.sum: Sand rammed round an ingot, or a brick, by a _Mechanical Press_ in a basin. Under a crucible's stream it takes _90 mB_ of metal; full, it _sets_, and an _ingot_ breaks out of the sand.
item.mcremix.sand_block_mold.tooltip.sum: Sand rammed round a block by a _Mechanical Press_ in a basin. Under a crucible's stream it takes _810 mB_ of metal; full, it _sets_, and a _block_ breaks out of the sand.
mcremix.goggles.crucible.every_column: Every column needs heat beneath it
block.mcremix.brass_steam_engine.tooltip: Create's steam engine in brass. It runs as Create's does, as fast and as strong from each level of its boiler, but goes only on _Brass Fluid Tanks_.
Create's steam engine in iron. It runs as Create's does, as fast and as strong from each level of its boiler, but goes only on _Iron Fluid Tanks_.
block.mcremix.steel_steam_engine.tooltip: Create's steam engine in steel. It runs as Create's does, as fast and as strong from each level of its boiler, but goes only on _Steel Fluid Tanks_. A steel boiler runs only on _pressurised steam_ piped in. It is _compact_, but _bursts_ unless a whistle vents the steam its engines do not use.
block.mcremix.iron_electric_pump.tooltip: Power Grid's _Electric Pump_ in iron. It pumps as Power Grid's does, faster the more _power_ it takes, but only up to _256 RPM_, as fast as iron mechanical pumps turn, and it _overheats_ on much more power than that takes. Holds fluids up to _Hot_. Left wet it _rusts_, and rusted through it _drips_; with the _rustedIronLeaks_ setting on it _leaks_ too, _1 mB a tick_ for every rusted block while fluid goes through. Scrape it with an _axe_, clean it with _acid_ or _wax_ it to stop that.
block.mcremix.steel_electric_pump.toolti: Power Grid's _Electric Pump_ in steel. It pumps as Power Grid's does, faster the more _power_ it takes, but only up to _512 RPM_, as fast as steel mechanical pumps turn, and it _overheats_ on much more power than that takes. Holds fluids up to _Searing_. Left wet it gets _spotted with rust_, but never worse, so it never leaks. _Wax_ it to keep it bright.
block.mcremix.aluminium_electric_pump.to: Power Grid's _Electric Pump_ in aluminium. It pumps as Power Grid's does, faster the more _power_ it takes, but only up to _512 RPM_, as fast as aluminium mechanical pumps turn, and it _overheats_ on much more power than that takes. Never weathers, but holds fluids only up to _Warm_: with anything _Hot_ inside or beside it (lava, fire, a lit Furnace, a Blaze Burner, molten metal) it _melts_ into rough aluminium.
block.mcremix.heat_sink.tooltip.summary: Finned aluminium. Bolted onto a _Power Grid_ device or an _aluminium_ or _titanium support_, it draws out the heat and sheds it, so the device takes _more power_ and the support turns _faster_ before either overheats. A _fan_ blowing through its fins makes it shed _far more_. Past _660 °C_ it _melts_, as aluminium does: titanium turning fast needs a _water cooler_.
block.mcremix.heat_sink.tooltip.behaviou: Its base goes against the block you place it on. Put _several_ on one block for more cooling.
mcremix.goggles.heat_sink.loose: Not bolted to anything that heats up
item.mcremix.red_mud.tooltip.summary: What's left when _bauxite_ dissolves: iron-red sludge. _Fire_ it in the Furnace into _red mud bricks_.
block.mcremix.electrolyser.tooltip.summa: Splits what is in a _basin_ or a _vat_ with a heavy current, carried into it by two _Carbon Electrodes_. A _Power Grid_ device: wire its _+_ and _-_ terminals across a source.
block.mcremix.electrolyser.tooltip.behav: Its electrodes go into the block you place it against: the _side of a basin_ or the _side of a vat_. A basin lets the _gases_ it makes escape; a vat keeps them for its pipes.
With a _Carbon Electrode_ in hand, fits it, the _anode_ (+) first. With an empty hand, takes one out.
Needs about _4 V_ to start. Past that the _current_, and how fast it splits, climb steeply, and so does its heat. The _anode burns away_ with the power through it, the _cathode_ a tenth as fast.
item.mcremix.carbon_electrode.tooltip.su: Coke and tar baked hard. Fitted in an _Electrolyser_, it carries the current into the liquid. It _burns away_ as it works, faster the _more power_ goes through it.
item.mcremix.unbaked_carbon_electrode.to: _Coal coke_ bound with _coal tar_ by a _press_. _Fire_ it _Hot_ in the Furnace to bake it into a _Carbon Electrode_.
mcremix.goggles.electrolyser.no_electrod: Fit two Carbon Electrodes to start
mcremix.goggles.electrolyser.no_vessel: Not on the side of a basin or a vat
mcremix.goggles.electrolyser.no_current: No current: wire it across 4 V or more
mcremix.goggles.vat.idle: Nothing to settle, ferment, split or mix
mcremix.goggles.vat.no_current: Waiting for current from its Electrolysers
mcremix.goggles.vat.waiting: %s items waiting for an inventory beside or under its scaffolding, or a funnel on it
item.mcremix.polyethylene_bushing.toolti: A waxy plastic sleeve for a shaft to turn in, pressed from _polyethylene pellets_ by a _press_ over a _heated_ basin. _Aluminium_ and _titanium_ supports take one.
mcremix.jei.fermenting.basin: In a basin with no heat under it and no mixer or press over it, or in a vat
mcremix.jei.fermenting.vat: A vat ferments a batch for each bucket it holds, up to 16 at once
block.mcremix.pvc_pipe.tooltip.summary: A thin white pipe that lies flat on a block face, like red alloy, and runs round _inside and outside corners_. Pumps push _twice as far_ through it. It only carries _Cold_ fluids: anything hotter makes it _sag and burst_.
block.mcremix.pvc_pipe.tooltip.behaviour: Runs on the same face join up, and it _rises to meet_ a pump, tank, basin or pipe beside it. Use a _wrench_ on a joint to cut it, and again to mend it.
block.mcremix.steel_furnace.tooltip.summ: A _Furnace_ cased in steel: it fires what a Furnace fires and works _fluids_ too, but burns only _fuel piped in from underneath_. Use _steel casing_ on a Furnace to make one.
block.mcremix.steel_furnace.tooltip.beha: Pipe or pour a fluid it works into its _front_, _sides_ or _top_ and it waits in the _feed tank_; what it gives waits there for a _pipe_ to draw it off. _Ethanol_ over _alumina_ in the chamber gives _ethylene_ at _Hot_; _ethylene dichloride_ cracks into _vinyl chloride_ and _hydrogen chloride_ at _Searing_.

Pump _wood spirit_, _ethanol_, _coal tar_, _hydrogen_ or _ethylene_ in from _underneath_ and _light_ it: the faster the pump, the _hotter_ it burns, up to what that fuel can reach, and anything faster is _lost_. Only _hydrogen_ and _ethylene_ reach _Blazing_. Unlit, gas fuel _escapes_ out of the front and liquid fuel _spills_ out. It takes no solid fuel, no heat from below and no bellows.
mcremix.goggles.steel_furnace.no_fuel: No fuel coming in from underneath
mcremix.goggles.steel_furnace.rich: Fed faster than it burns: past %s mB a tick is lost
mcremix.goggles.steel_furnace.backing_up: %s backing up: it has nowhere to spill
mcremix.goggles.furnace.unlit: Not lit: use flint and steel or a fire charge
mcremix.furnace.nothing_to_light: There is no fuel in it to catch
mcremix.steel_furnace.nothing_to_light: Nothing to catch: pipe fuel in from underneath first
mcremix.steel_furnace.piped_fuel_only: A Steel Furnace only burns fuel piped in from underneath
mcremix.goggles.bellows.sealed: A Steel Furnace is sealed: air does nothing for it
mcremix.jei.steel_furnace_fuel.piped: Piped into a lit Steel Furnace from underneath and burnt as it comes; what comes faster than it burns is lost
mcremix.jei.steel_furnace_fuel.pump: A pump turning at %s RPM moves that much
mcremix.jei.steel_furnace.catalyst: Lies in the chamber; one wears away every %s mB
mcremix.goggles.vat_mixer.other_material: Does not fit a vat of this material
mcremix.goggles.vat_mixer.idle: Nothing in the vat to mix
mcremix.jei.vat_mixing.vat: Only in a vat, which holds gases: a basin lets them go
mcremix.jei.vat_mixing.mixer: A mixer used on a vat's side goes on as its vat form. Copper, iron, steel and aluminium mixers each stir vats of their own metal; Create's mixer works only over basins, and no mixer fits a brass vat
mcremix.jei.vat_mixing.batches: Each mixer stirs four batches at a time; a big vat wants several
block.mcremix.spark_plug.tooltip.summary: Screws into the _side of a Furnace or Steel Furnace_ and _lights it_ with a spark. It sparks only with about _1,000 V_ across it, so it wants a _transformer_ stepping the voltage up.
block.mcremix.spark_plug.tooltip.behavio: Goes on any side of a furnace _but its front_, low by the firebox. Its _+_ is the copper cap, its _-_ the lug on the iron shell.

Sparks the whole time _900 V_ or more are across it, lit furnace or not, drawing only about _10 mA_, and _lights the furnace_ as soon as there is fuel in it to catch. Put a _switch_ or _relay_ in its circuit to decide when. It _never wears out_.
mcremix.goggles.spark_plug.too_low: Not sparking: it wants %s V or more
block.mcremix.pressurizer.tooltip.summar: Squeezes the fluid piped into it, its _shaft_ working a pump into the _pressure vessel_ on top. _Speed is pressure_: each job needs a _least speed_, and faster than that is quicker. It needs _room above_ for its vessel.
block.mcremix.pressurizer.tooltip.behavi: _Ethylene_ into _polyethylene pellets_ at _512 RPM_, with _heat_ under it. _Vinyl chloride_ into _PVC resin_ at _256 RPM_, heated or not. _Water_ into _pressurised steam_ at _128 RPM_, over a _Hot_ fire.
It is all a _steel boiler_ runs on: every _10 mB a tick_ piped in is a boiler level. It makes _20 mB a tick at 128 RPM_, twice that at 256 and _80 at 512_.

Fluid goes in at any of the _four sides_ of its _vessel_, which reaches out to meet each pipe, and what it makes is drawn off the same sides: fluid by _pumps_, items by _funnels_ or an _empty hand_. Its _shaft_ goes in at _either side_ of the lower block, left or right of the dial.
Reads the _pressure_, which is how fast it turns: from nothing to the _top speed_ of its metal, each mark a quarter of it. Past top speed the needle is in the _red_.
block.mcremix.titanium_pressurizer.toolt: The Pressurizer in _titanium_: it takes up to _2048 RPM_ where the steel one stops at _512_, so it squeezes up to _four times as fast_. Like all titanium it _heats as it turns_ and _burns_ if nothing cools it: past about _128 RPM_ give it a _Water Cooler_.

The same as the steel one: _ethylene_ into _polyethylene pellets_ at _512 RPM_ over _heat_, _vinyl chloride_ into _PVC resin_ at _256 RPM_, _water_ into _pressurised steam_ at _128 RPM_ over a _Hot_ fire. Twice as fast is twice as quick, and steam comes at up to _320 mB a tick_ at 2048.
Heat turns it _gold_, _purple_ and _blue_ for good; _hydrochloric acid_ strips it back.
mcremix.jei.pressurizing.speed: Its least speed, %s RPM: nothing happens slower, and twice as fast is twice as quick
mcremix.jei.pressurizing.heat: The heat under the Pressurizer, at least; any hotter works the same
mcremix.goggles.pressurizer.idle: Idle: pipe in what to squeeze
mcremix.goggles.pressurizer.too_cold: Too cold: this needs %s heat under it
mcremix.goggles.pressurizer.full: Full: draw off what it made
block.mcremix.water_cooler.tooltip.summa: A heat sink with a _water jacket_. Bolted onto a _Power Grid_ device or an _aluminium_ or _titanium support_, it draws the heat into _water_ piped through it, faster than any heat sink, and gives it back as _warm water_. _Cold water_ cools twice as fast, and _coolant_ three times as fast, coming out _hot_.
block.mcremix.water_cooler.tooltip.behav: Its base goes against the block you place it on. Pipe water or coolant in on any other face, and pipe what comes out away, or it stops when it is full.
block.mcremix.radiator.tooltip.summary: Thin aluminium fins on copper tubes. It chills any _water_ into _cold water_, and _hot coolant_ back into _coolant_: slowly on its own, _much faster_ with an encased fan blowing through it. Cold water and coolant pass straight through.
block.mcremix.radiator.tooltip.behaviour: It faces you, or the radiator you place it against. Radiators _side by side_ facing the same way _join_ into one panel that shares what it holds, with pipes on its front or back anywhere. Every block chills its share, so a bigger panel chills more, and a _fan under each column_ blowing up cools the whole column.
mcremix.goggles.water_cooler.loose: Not bolted to anything that heats up
mcremix.goggles.water_cooler.full: What it gives back has nowhere to go
mcremix.goggles.radiator.full: Full: what it gives out has nowhere to go
mcremix.goggles.radiator.fans: Fans blowing through it: %sx as fast
mcremix.goggles.radiator.fanned_blocks: Fans blowing through %s of its %s blocks
mcremix.goggles.radiator.still: Still air: a fan blowing through it chills much faster
mcremix.jei.info.water_cooler: Bolt it onto a Power Grid device or an aluminium or titanium support and pipe water, cold water or coolant through it. It takes heat in step with how far above the air that is: on water 15 W for each degree, on cold water twice that, on coolant three times. Water comes out warm, coolant hot.
mcremix.jei.info.radiator: Chills any water into cold water, and hot coolant back into coolant: half a millibucket a tick for each block in still air, and much faster with a fan blowing through it. Radiators side by side join into a panel. Cold water and coolant pass straight through.
mcremix.jei.info.warm_water: What a Water Cooler gives back for water. A Radiator chills it into cold water. Poured out, it is only water.
mcremix.jei.info.cold_water: Taken by bucket, pump or hose pulley in any snowy biome or wherever else it snows, or chilled by a Radiator. In a Water Cooler it takes heat twice as fast as water. Poured out, it is only water.
mcremix.jei.info.coolant: Glycol and water. In a Water Cooler it takes heat three times as fast as water and comes out as hot coolant, which a Radiator cools back. It never wears out, so keep it going round a loop of coolers and radiators.
mcremix.jei.info.hot_coolant: What a Water Cooler gives back for coolant. A Radiator cools it back into coolant. Poured out, it is only coolant.
item.mcremix.titanium_ingot.tooltip.summ: Light, strong and slow to give up its heat. Its supports turn up to _2048 RPM_ with _no drag_, and its shafts and cogs take _any load_, but its supports need _twice the cooling_ aluminium's do, and _burn_ past _1000 °C_.
block.mcremix.titanium_casing.tooltip.su: Crafted from a _titanium sheet_, a stripped log and _polyethylene_, since every titanium support needs polyethylene. Titanium gearboxes, clutches, gearshifts and chain drives are built on it.
block.mcremix.black_sand.tooltip.summary: _Basalt_ crushed fine: dark grains of iron ore with a little _rutile_ among them. Power Grid's _electromagnet_ pulls the iron out and leaves the rutile.
item.mcremix.rutile.tooltip.summary: Titanium's ore, red-black crystals of _titanium dioxide_. Pressed with _coal coke_ and _coal tar_ into _briquettes_, which _chlorine_ run over in a _Steel Furnace_ at _Blazing_ heat turns into _titanium tetrachloride_.
item.mcremix.salt.tooltip.summary: Boiled out of _salt water_ in a _heated basin_ with nothing working it. Melted in a _crucible_, an _Electrolyser_ splits it into _sodium_ and _chlorine_.
item.mcremix.titanium_sponge.tooltip.sum: Titanium as sodium leaves it, porous and full of salt. An _Arc Furnace_ melts it down into _ingots_.
item.mcremix.titanium_dioxide.tooltip.su: The white powder burnt titanium crumbles into. It does for _rutile_ again, and makes _white dye_.
block.mcremix.titanium_plating.tooltip.s: Titanium sheets riveted over a block, for building with. Fired in a _Furnace_ it takes on titanium's _temper colours_ for good: _gold_ at _Hot_, _purple_ at _Searing_, _blue_ at _Blazing_, never going back to a lighter one. _Hydrochloric acid_ strips the colour off.
block.mcremix.gold_tinted_titanium_plati: Titanium sheets riveted over a block, for building with. Fired in a _Furnace_ it takes on titanium's _temper colours_ for good: _gold_ at _Hot_, _purple_ at _Searing_, _blue_ at _Blazing_, never going back to a lighter one. _Hydrochloric acid_ strips the colour off.
block.mcremix.purple_tinted_titanium_pla: Titanium sheets riveted over a block, for building with. Fired in a _Furnace_ it takes on titanium's _temper colours_ for good: _gold_ at _Hot_, _purple_ at _Searing_, _blue_ at _Blazing_, never going back to a lighter one. _Hydrochloric acid_ strips the colour off.
block.mcremix.blue_tinted_titanium_plati: Titanium sheets riveted over a block, for building with. Fired in a _Furnace_ it takes on titanium's _temper colours_ for good: _gold_ at _Hot_, _purple_ at _Searing_, _blue_ at _Blazing_, never going back to a lighter one. _Hydrochloric acid_ strips the colour off.
item.mcremix.rutile_briquette.tooltip.su: _Rutile_ and _coal coke_ bound with _coal tar_ by a press. _Chlorine_ run over it in a _Steel Furnace_ at _Blazing_ heat comes off as _titanium tetrachloride_, the coke taking the rutile's oxygen; one wears away for each batch.
block.mcremix.arc_furnace.tooltip.summar: A _Power Grid_ device. It strikes an _arc_ from one _Carbon Electrode_ down through what lies in its copper hearth and back up the other, melting _titanium sponge_ into _ingots_. Molten titanium dissolves any other crucible, so the hearth is copper, kept cool by _water_.
block.mcremix.arc_furnace.tooltip.behavi: The arc is a heavy load of _a quarter ohm_, with no + or -: _20 V_ drive _80 A_, _1.6 kW_. It melts only from _400 W_, each sponge taking _16 kJ_, and its hearth sheds only _150 W_ by itself, so it _overheats_ unless a _water cooler_ takes the heat: one on water holds it to about _2.5 kW_.

A _Carbon Electrode_ goes into an empty holder and _sponge_ into the hearth; an empty hand takes out the _ingots_, then the sponge, then an electrode. Funnels and arms put them in; hoppers take the ingots out. Both electrodes burn away as it works.
mcremix.goggles.arc_furnace.nothing_to_m: Nothing in the hearth to melt
mcremix.goggles.arc_furnace.full: Full: take out what it has made
mcremix.goggles.arc_furnace.too_weak: Too weak an arc to melt anything: it takes %s W
mcremix.jei.arc_furnace.energy.note: Each takes that much energy, so the more power through the arc, the faster it melts
mcremix.jei.arc_furnace.weak: Under %s W the arc only warms the hearth
mcremix.jei.boiling.basin: In a basin over a fed Blaze Burner or a Furnace burning Searing or hotter, with no mixer or press over it
